text:
One script hammered my API and took everyone down. I had no logs to explain why.

That wasn't a feature bug — I'd skipped the concerns that touch every service:

• Rate limiting — token bucket for bursts; reject before one client sinks the fleet
• Observability — logs, metrics, traces; you can't fix what you can't see
• Security — authn ≠ authz; least privilege from day one
• CDNs — cache shared content at the edge, never personalized responses

Cross-cutting concerns don't demo well. They decide whether production survives real traffic.

Last fundamentals post in my System Design series.
